blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Spending Governance**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Economics, § Spending Governance
blocks.md: When a coordinator admits concurrent sub-agents or child tasks, simple balance checks collapse under race conditions. If two children inspect the remaining free balance simultaneously before either records a reservation, both admission checks succeed, yet their combined liability immediately breaches the authorized task budget. Task cancellation introduces a second concurrency bug: returning a stopped child's allocation to the free pool while its remote service call remains billable allows another worker to spend funds that are already committed to third-party infrastructure. The harness already solved this for one trajectory.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Liability bounds and admission
- Budget conservation across descendants
- Spending alarms and admission limits
